findings: DuplicateScannerTests defines eight tests covering basic equality/negative, nested folders, injected recoverable move, progress stage presence, keeper depth and override, changed extra and missing keeper. It does not test keeper content replacement, same-size restored-time cache edits, hardlink aliases, traversal limits or cancellation diagnostics. Tests were source-read, not executed.

ExtractedArchiveScanner verifies each archive entry using relative path and uncompressed size only, without CRC or byte/hash comparison. Equal-size different extracted contents can be classified as already extracted; trash recheck repeats the same weak predicate.

ZIP listing parses textual unzip -l -qq output and trims whitespace, skipping unparseable lines and metadata entries. This is not a complete ZIP central-directory parser and can alter whitespace-bearing names.

run accepts nonempty output even when process exits unsuccessfully, including data truncated at 4 MB or deadline break. Partial listings can therefore be treated as sufficient entries without a completeness flag.

Process deadline is checked only after blocking read returns, and waitUntilExit after terminate has no independent bound. A silent or termination-resistant child is not reliably constrained by the nominal 20-second timeout.

Entry paths reject absolute and dot-dot components, but verification does not resolve physical containment or explicitly reject symlink ancestors. Source-only observation; no crafted archive or deletion was executed.
ZIP discovery is limited to top-level and managed category roots and 20000 parsed entries; those omissions are returned without a diagnostic report.
